title: CRM Data Pipeline
summary: A customer data pipeline joins what users do in the product with what sales knows in the CRM. Product events and CRM record changes stream into a warehouse, are stitched into one customer profile, and the resulting signals (lead score, last active, PQL) are synced back into the CRM so sales can act on them.

walkthrough.title: User action is tracked
walkthrough.text: A signed-in user upgrades their plan. The SDK sends a track event and an identify call linking the browser's anonymousId to the userId.

walkthrough.title: Validate and enqueue
walkthrough.text: The collector checks the event against the tracking plan, drops duplicates by messageId, enriches it, and writes it to Kafka keyed by user.

walkthrough.title: CRM change captured
walkthrough.text: Meanwhile a sales rep updates the Contact's account owner. Salesforce emits a change event; the CDC connector checkpoints its replayId and publishes the change to Kafka.

walkthrough.title: Land in the warehouse
walkthrough.text: A sink connector loads both topics into append-only raw tables in the warehouse, in micro-batches every minute or so.

walkthrough.title: Resolve identity and model
walkthrough.text: Scheduled dbt models link anonymousId, userId, email, and CRM ContactId into one canonical customer, then compute traits like lead score and product-qualified-lead status.

walkthrough.title: Sync back to the CRM
walkthrough.text: Reverse ETL diffs customer_360 against the last sync and upserts only the changed fields into pipeline-owned CRM fields, where reps and routing rules see them.

data.label: Product App & Web Tracking

input.name: User interactions
input.type: DOM / app events, login → identify(userId, traits)

output.name: Tracked events (batched)
output.type: JSON: { type: "track" | "identify", event, anonymousId, userId?, properties, messageId, timestamp }

responsibilities: Captures behavioural events (signed up, feature used, plan upgraded) against a stable anonymousId cookie.
Calls identify() at login so earlier anonymous activity can be linked to the known user.
Queues and retries in the background so tracking never blocks or slows the UI.

failureModes.scenario: Ad blockers and browser privacy features drop client events
failureModes.impact: 10 to 30% of browser events silently go missing; funnels undercount.
failureModes.mitigation: Send business-critical events (signup, purchase) server-side, not from the browser.

failureModes.scenario: Device clock is wrong
failureModes.impact: Events land out of order or on the wrong day.
failureModes.mitigation: Record sentAt alongside timestamp; the collector corrects skew using receivedAt.

failureModes.scenario: PII leaks into event properties (e.g. email in a URL)
failureModes.impact: Personal data spreads into systems not approved to hold it.
failureModes.mitigation: Property allowlists in the tracking plan; redact known PII patterns at the collector.

data.label: Event Collector API

input.name: Event batch
input.type: HTTP POST /v1/batch { batch: Event[] } + write key

output.name: Kafka record
output.type: key = anonymousId | userId, value = Event (Avro) + { receivedAt, geo, userAgent }

responsibilities: Authenticates the source's write key and validates each event against the tracking-plan schema.
Deduplicates by messageId and enriches with server receive time, IP-derived geo, and parsed user agent.
Partitions by user key so each user's events stay in order downstream.

failureModes.scenario: A new app release sends events that break the schema
failureModes.impact: Malformed rows reach the warehouse and break dashboards.
failureModes.mitigation: Route violations to a quarantine topic; alert when the violation rate spikes.

failureModes.scenario: Kafka is unreachable
failureModes.impact: Events are dropped if the collector answers 2xx without persisting them.
failureModes.mitigation: Return 503 so SDKs retry, and buffer to local disk for short outages.

failureModes.scenario: Client retries resend the same batch
failureModes.impact: Events are double-counted.
failureModes.mitigation: Dedupe on messageId within a time window, and again with MERGE in the warehouse.

data.label: CRM (System of Record)

input.name: Rep edits
input.type: UI: Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity updates

input.name: Reverse-ETL upserts
input.type: Bulk API: Contact { External_Id__c, Lead_Score__c, PQL__c }

output.name: Change event
output.type: JSON: { ChangeEventHeader: { entityName, changeType, recordIds[], commitTimestamp, changedFields[] }, …fields }

responsibilities: System of record for accounts, contacts, leads, and opportunities, owned and edited by sales.
Emits a change event for every create, update, delete, and undelete.
Enforces org-wide API limits (a daily call quota shared by every integration).

failureModes.scenario: Daily API quota exhausted
failureModes.impact: The pipeline and every other integration (email, CPQ, support) stop until the quota resets.
failureModes.mitigation: Per-integration budgets, Bulk API for large reads and writes, alerts on remaining calls.

failureModes.scenario: Duplicate records are merged in the CRM
failureModes.impact: The losing record ID vanishes; downstream keeps a ghost contact with its history.
failureModes.mitigation: Handle merge events (MasterRecordId) and re-point history to the surviving ID.

failureModes.scenario: An admin renames or deletes a custom field
failureModes.impact: The connector errors, or the column silently becomes null.
failureModes.mitigation: Schema-change alerts, and a data contract with Sales Ops for fields the pipeline relies on.

data.label: CRM Change Data Capture Connector

output.name: Kafka record
output.type: key = recordId, value = { op: "c" | "u" | "d", after, changedFields[], ts }

responsibilities: Subscribes to the CRM change stream and checkpoints the last replayId so it resumes without gaps.
Runs a full historical backfill with bulk queries first, then switches to incremental changes.
Maps CRM objects, including custom fields and soft deletes, into typed records.

failureModes.scenario: Connector is down longer than the CRM's event retention (72h for Salesforce)
failureModes.impact: Missed changes can no longer be replayed; the warehouse silently diverges.
failureModes.mitigation: Alert on checkpoint age well before retention; fall back to a full re-sync.

failureModes.scenario: Formula and rollup fields change without emitting events
failureModes.impact: Derived fields in the warehouse go stale.
failureModes.mitigation: Periodic reconciliation query on SystemModstamp for affected objects.

failureModes.scenario: Two updates to one record arrive out of order
failureModes.impact: An older value overwrites a newer one.
failureModes.mitigation: Key by recordId (same partition), and apply only if commitTimestamp is newer.

data.label: Event Stream
responsibilities: Durable, per-partition-ordered buffer that decouples producers from slower consumers.
Retains data (e.g. 7 days) so any consumer can rewind and replay after a bug fix.
Schema registry blocks producers from publishing incompatible schema changes.

failureModes.scenario: Consumer lag keeps growing
failureModes.impact: Warehouse and CRM fields fall hours behind reality.
failureModes.mitigation: Alert on lag in seconds, not offsets; autoscale sink consumers.

failureModes.scenario: One huge customer creates a hot partition
failureModes.impact: One partition saturates while others idle; throughput caps out.
failureModes.mitigation: Key by user rather than account; add salting for known heavy keys.

failureModes.scenario: Incompatible schema change reaches consumers
failureModes.impact: Every consumer of the topic crashes on deserialization.
failureModes.mitigation: Registry compatibility mode set to BACKWARD; contract tests in producer CI.

data.label: Data Warehouse

output.name: Modeled tables
output.type: SQL: marts.customer_360 { canonical_id, email, account_id, lead_score, is_pql, last_active_at, mrr }

responsibilities: Lands raw data append-only with a load timestamp, so any model can be rebuilt from scratch.
Hosts layered models (raw → staging → marts) as the single source for analytics.
Serves BI dashboards, analysts, and the reverse-ETL sync.

failureModes.scenario: Sink retries load the same batch twice
failureModes.impact: Inflated event counts and revenue metrics.
failureModes.mitigation: Load with MERGE on messageId / recordId instead of plain INSERT.

failureModes.scenario: Late-arriving events (offline mobile clients)
failureModes.impact: Yesterday's metrics change after they were reported.
failureModes.mitigation: Incremental models with a lookback window; label recent days as provisional.

failureModes.scenario: Full-refresh models on growing tables
failureModes.impact: Compute cost and run time grow without limit.
failureModes.mitigation: Incremental materializations, clustering, and per-query cost alerts.

data.label: Identity Resolution & Modeling

output.name: Identity graph
output.type: SQL: identity_graph { anonymous_id, user_id, email, crm_contact_id, canonical_id }

responsibilities: Links anonymousId, userId, email, and CRM ContactId into connected groups, each with one canonical_id.
Applies survivorship rules: the CRM wins for name and title, the product wins for activity and plan.
Computes traits (lead score, PQL flag, MRR) guarded by dbt tests (unique, not_null, relationships).

failureModes.scenario: Over-merging through a shared identifier (support@, shared device)
failureModes.impact: Customers from different companies collapse into one profile and data leaks between them.
failureModes.mitigation: Blocklist generic emails and devices; cap identity-group size and alert on outliers.

failureModes.scenario: A failing dbt test halts the DAG
failureModes.impact: Marts stop refreshing; the CRM keeps stale scores.
failureModes.mitigation: Classify tests as blocking or warn; alert on mart freshness, not just job status.

failureModes.scenario: Scoring logic changes in a PR
failureModes.impact: Lead routing to sales reps shifts overnight without anyone noticing.
failureModes.mitigation: In CI, diff key metrics such as the lead-score distribution against production before merge.

data.label: Reverse ETL (Activation)

input.name: Model snapshot
input.type: SQL: SELECT … FROM marts.customer_360, diffed against last sync

output.name: CRM upserts
output.type: Bulk API upsert: Contact by External_Id__c { Lead_Score__c, Last_Active__c, PQL__c }

responsibilities: Diffs the current model against the previous sync so only changed rows use API calls.
Upserts by external ID into dedicated, pipeline-owned CRM fields in API-limit-sized batches.
Records per-row failures (e.g. CRM validation rules) and retries or reports them.

failureModes.scenario: Feedback loop: the sync's own writes come back through CDC
failureModes.impact: Each sync triggers changes, which trigger another sync; API quota drains.
failureModes.mitigation: Write only to pipeline-owned fields and filter those fields out of the CDC path.

failureModes.scenario: Field mapping overwrites rep-entered data
failureModes.impact: Sales loses trust in the CRM and in the data team.
failureModes.mitigation: Never write to rep-owned fields; preview diffs (dry run) before enabling a sync.

failureModes.scenario: CRM validation rules reject some rows
failureModes.impact: Partial sync reported as success; some reps see stale scores.
failureModes.mitigation: Surface row-level errors; alert when the rejection rate passes a threshold.
